sections.title: Explanation
sections.body:
> **In one line:** HAProxy (High Availability Proxy) is an open-source, high-performance Layer 4/TCP and Layer 7/HTTP load balancer known for reliability, granular ACL-based routing, a rich stats page, SSL termination with SNI routing, and hot config reloads — widely deployed in front of high-throughput databases and web tiers.

HAProxy was created in 2001 by Willy Tarreau and has earned a reputation as the most reliable software load balancer in production. Where NGINX is the swiss army knife (web server + proxy + LB), HAProxy is purely a load balancer — it doesn't serve static files, it doesn't do URI rewriting beyond simple patterns, and it doesn't have NGINX's module ecosystem. What it does, it does exceptionally well: sustain millions of requests per second on a single box with sub-millisecond latency, never crash under load (HAProxy's bug rate is famously low), and provide granular per-request routing via ACLs (Access Control Lists). Real-world deployments include Stack Overflow (HAProxy in front of their entire web tier and PostgreSQL), Reddit (HAProxy for API routing), Airbnb (HAProxy for SSL termination and L7 routing), GitHub (HAProxy for the github.com frontend), and Tumblr (HAProxy handling 10+ billion requests/day). When a site needs "just a load balancer" with maximum reliability, HAProxy is the default choice.

The **ACL (Access Control List) system** is HAProxy's signature feature. An ACL is a named condition that matches something about the request: `path_beg /api/`, `hdr(host) -i api.example.com`, `src 192.168.0.0/16`, `ssl_fc` (request came in over SSL), `http_auth` (user is authenticated), and dozens more. ACLs are combined with `if`/`unless` clauses on `use_backend`, `redirect`, `http-request`, and other directives, allowing extremely fine-grained routing. For example: `use_backend api_v2 if { path_beg /api/v2/ }` routes /api/v2/ requests to a different backend pool; `use_backend mobile if { req.hdr(User-Agent) -i -m sub mobile }` routes mobile clients to a mobile-optimized backend; `http-request deny if { src -f /etc/haproxy/blocklist.txt }` blocks requests from blacklisted IPs. This declarative, composable ACL system is more powerful than NGINX's `location` blocks for complex routing, and it's the reason HAProxy is often used as an API gateway — you can express arbitrarily complex routing rules in config without writing Lua code.

HAProxy supports both **Layer 4 (TCP) and Layer 7 (HTTP)** modes. In TCP mode (`mode tcp`), HAProxy proxies raw bytes — useful for databases (PostgreSQL on 5432, Redis on 6379, MySQL on 3306), proprietary binary protocols, and TLS passthrough (where HAProxy forwards encrypted bytes without terminating SSL, using SNI to route). In HTTP mode (`mode http`), HAProxy parses HTTP, can read/modify headers, do path-based routing, manipulate cookies (for sticky sessions), and serve stats. The choice depends on the workload: HTTP traffic in HTTP mode (for the rich features), databases and TLS passthrough in TCP mode. A common pattern is one HAProxy in TCP mode in front of a PostgreSQL cluster (load-balancing reads across replicas, with a separate virtual server for writes to the primary), and another HAProxy in HTTP mode in front of the web tier.

The **stats page** is one of HAProxy's most loved features. Enabled with `stats enable`, `stats uri /haproxy?stats`, and `stats auth admin:password`, it provides a real-time HTML dashboard showing per-frontend and per-backend request rates, connection counts, response time percentiles, server health (UP/DOWN/MAINT), session counts, and error rates. The stats page is interactive — you can put a backend into MAINT mode (drain), set its weight, or kill active sessions from the UI. In a production incident, the stats page is the first place operators look: "is the backend saturated?" "is one server failing?" "are sessions queuing?". NGINX's open-source stats are limited (you need NGINX Plus or third-party modules like `stub_status` for any visibility); HAProxy's stats are best-in-class out of the box. The stats data is also available in CSV and Prometheus formats for integration with Grafana, Datadog, and other monitoring tools.

**SSL termination and SNI routing** are core features. HAProxy terminates TLS using OpenSSL, with cert-per-SNI support: `bind *:443 ssl crt /etc/haproxy/certs/api.example.com.pem crt /etc/haproxy/certs/admin.example.com.pem` lets HAProxy serve multiple certificates on the same port, selecting the right one based on the SNI in the ClientHello. For TLS passthrough (where HAProxy doesn't decrypt, just routes encrypted bytes based on SNI), use `mode tcp` with `tcp-request inspect-delay 5s` and `use_backend api_server if { req.ssl_sni -i api.example.com }` — this is useful when backends terminate their own TLS (e.g., for end-to-end encryption) but you still want to route by hostname. HAProxy's SNI-based routing is more flexible than NGINX's, because HAProxy can mix passthrough and termination in the same config (NGINX requires separate `server` blocks). Stack Overflow uses HAProxy's SNI passthrough for some internal services where end-to-end TLS is required.

The **hot config reload** (`systemctl reload haproxy` or `haproxy -f /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg -c && systemctl reload haproxy`) is one of HAProxy's operational strengths. HAProxy's reload process forks a new process with the new config, atomically transfers the listening sockets (via `SO_REUSEPORT` or inherit-fd mechanism) from the old process to the new, and the old process drains in-flight connections before exiting. The result is zero-downtime reloads with no dropped connections — even mid-handshake TLS connections are preserved because the socket handoff happens at the kernel level. This is critical for high-throughput production environments where reloads must not interrupt traffic. HAProxy also supports a runtime API (Unix socket on `/run/haproxy/admin.sock`) for live changes without reload: add/remove servers, set weights, enable/disable backends, clear stick-table entries — all via plain-text commands like `echo "set server api/backend1 state drain" | socat /run/haproxy/admin.sock`. This runtime API is what Kubernetes ingress controllers and Consul-template use to dynamically update HAProxy's backend pools without reloads.

The **load-balancing algorithms** are another strength. HAProxy supports `roundrobin` (default, weighted), `static-rr` (faster but no dynamic weight changes), `leastconn` (lowest active connections, good for long-lived connections), `source` (source IP hash, for sticky-by-IP), `uri` (URL hash, for cache locality), `hdr(name)` (header hash), and `random` (random with optional power-of-two-choices for better distribution). The `roundrobin` algorithm supports dynamic weights — you can change a server's weight at runtime via the admin socket, and HAProxy immediately adjusts traffic distribution. **Slow-start** (`slowstart 30s`) ramps up a server's weight gradually after it comes back from being down, preventing a thundering herd of queued requests from swamping a freshly-warmed backend. **Health checks** in HAProxy are sophisticated: active checks (`check` directive on a `server` line, with `inter`, `rise`, `fall` parameters for interval/thresholds), passive checks (`observe layer4` / `observe layer7` to mark servers down based on real traffic failures), and agent checks (a separate TCP agent on the backend that HAProxy polls for app-level health). This combination of active + passive + agent checks is more nuanced than NGINX's open-source offering.

The trade-off versus NGINX is the inverse of NGINX's strengths. HAProxy has no static file serving (you need NGINX or a CDN in front for that), no built-in HTTP/2 (until HAProxy 2.0 in 2019, which added HTTP/2 support; HTTP/3 is still maturing), and a smaller module ecosystem. But for pure load balancing — especially in front of databases, for high-throughput L4, or for any deployment that values the stats page and runtime API — HAProxy is the better choice. Many sites run both: NGINX at the edge for SSL/HTTP/static, HAProxy behind it for L4 backend routing. Reddit, Stack Overflow, and GitHub all use this pattern. HAProxy 2.0+ also added a "data plane API" (REST API for runtime config, similar to NGINX Plus's API), making it more cloud-native and easier to integrate with Kubernetes and service meshes.

live weight changes] style ACL fill:#eef,stroke:#00a style Stats fill:#efe,stroke:#0a0 style RuntimeAPI fill:#fee,stroke:#a00 ``` ### ASCII Diagram ``` HAPROXY ARCHITECTURE (single process, event-driven, ACL-based): +---------------------------+ client ---HTTPS--->| HAProxy | | - SSL termination (OpenSSL)| | - parse HTTP request | | - evaluate ACLs | +-------------+---------------+ | +---------------------+---------------------+ v v v +-----------+ +-----------+ +-----------+ | frontend | | frontend | | frontend | | https_in | | tcp_pg | | tcp_redis | | (mode http) | (mode tcp) | (mode tcp) | +-----+-----+ +-----+-----+ +-----+-----+ | | | use_backend if ACL use_backend use_backend | | | v v v +-----------+ +-----------+ +-----------+ | backend | | backend | | backend | | api_v2 | | pg_pool | | redis_pool| | RR + chk | | leastconn | | RR | +-----+-----+ +-----+-----+ +-----+-----+ | | | +-----+-----+ +-----+-----+ +-----+-----+ | srv1 srv2 | | pg1 pg2 pg3| | r1 r2 r3 r4| | srv3 (w=2)| | (master=* )| +-----+------+ +-----------+ +------------+ STATS PAGE (per backend, live): +------------------+--------+------+------+------+-------+------+ | backend | req/s | conn | errs | 5xx | p99 |state | +------------------+--------+------+------+------+-------+------+ | api_v2 | 12,500 | 340 | 0 | 2 | 18ms | OK | | api_v1 | 45,200 | 890 | 1 | 12 | 35ms | OK | | srv3 (api_v1) | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | DOWN | +------------------+--------+------+------+------+-------+------+ RUNTIME API (admin.sock, no reload): $ echo "set server api_v1/srv3 state drain" | socat /run/haproxy/admin.sock - $ echo "set server api_v1/srv3 weight 50%" | socat /run/haproxy/admin.sock - $ echo "show servers state api_v1" | socat /run/haproxy/admin.sock - ``` ### Walkthrough 1. A client opens a TLS connection to HAProxy on port 443. HAProxy terminates SSL (selecting the certificate by SNI), parses the HTTP request, and evaluates ACLs in the configured `frontend` block: `path_beg /api/v2/`? `hdr(host) admin.*`? `src` in blocklist? Each ACL is a named condition; the first matching `use_backend` directive routes the request. 2. The chosen `backend` block applies its load-balancing algorithm (`roundrobin`, `leastconn`, `source`, etc.) to pick a server from the pool. Active health checks continuously poll each server (default `inter 2s rise 2 fall 3` — check every 2s, need 2 successes to be UP, 3 failures to be DOWN); passive checks (`observe layer7`) mark a server down immediately if real traffic returns errors. Slow-start ramps a freshly-recovered server's weight over 30s to avoid thundering herd. 3. The request is proxied to the chosen server; the response is streamed back to the client. All metrics (request rate, connection count, error count, latency percentiles, server health) are updated in real-time and visible on the stats page (`/haproxy?stats`) and queryable via the runtime API (`/run/haproxy/admin.sock`), enabling live operational changes (drain a server, change weights) without config reloads.

sections.title: Code
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- frontend https_in bind *:443 ssl crt /etc/haproxy/certs/api.pem mode http acl is_api_v2 path_beg /api/v2/ acl is_admin hdr(host) -i admin.example.com…
- Tiny ACL evaluator: path_beg, hdr(host) -i, src -f.
- Mock HAProxy: parses a small subset of haproxy.cfg, then routes
- Incoming requests by ACLs to backends with round-robin / leastconn.
- Demonstrates: ACL evaluation, weighted RR, active health check,
- Runtime API for live weight changes (no reload).
- Sample haproxy.cfg (parsed by our mock)
- Runtime API: change weight without reload

**Defines:** `HAProxyConfig`, `HAProxy`

```python
# Mock HAProxy: parses a small subset of haproxy.cfg, then routes
# incoming requests by ACLs to backends with round-robin / leastconn.
# Demonstrates: ACL evaluation, weighted RR, active health check,
# runtime API for live weight changes (no reload).

import re
import time
import random
from collections import defaultdict

# ---- Sample haproxy.cfg (parsed by our mock) ----
HAPROXY_CFG = """
frontend https_in
    bind *:443 ssl crt /etc/haproxy/certs/api.pem
    mode http
    acl is_api_v2   path_beg /api/v2/
    acl is_admin    hdr(host) -i admin.example.com
    acl is_blocked  src -f /etc/haproxy/blocked.txt
    http-request deny if is_blocked
    use_backend api_v2  if is_api_v2
    use_backend admin   if is_admin
    default_backend api_v1

backend api_v1
    mode http
    balance roundrobin
    option httpchk GET /healthz
    server s1 10.0.0.1:8080 check weight 1
    server s2 10.0.0.2:8080 check weight 1
    server s3 10.0.0.3:8080 check weight 2

backend api_v2
    mode http
    balance leastconn
    server v2_1 10.0.1.1:8080 check
    server v2_2 10.0.1.2:8080 check
"""

class HAProxyConfig:
    def __init__(self, cfg_text):
        self.frontends = {}   # name -> {acls: {name: cond}, rules: [(acl_logic, backend)], default}
        self.backends = {}    # name -> {balance, servers: [(name, ip:port, weight, healthy)]}
        self._parse(cfg_text)

    def _parse(self, text):
        cur_block, cur_name = None, None
        for line in text.split('\n'):
            line = line.strip()
            if not line or line.startswith('#'):
                continue
            m = re.match(r'(frontend|backend)\s+(\S+)', line)
            if m:
                cur_block, cur_name = m.group(1), m.group(2)
                if cur_block == 'frontend':
                    self.frontends[cur_name] = {'acls': {}, 'rules': [], 'default': None}
                else:
                    self.backends[cur_name] = {'balance': 'roundrobin', 'servers': []}
                continue
            if cur_block == 'frontend':
                m = re.match(r'acl\s+(\S+)\s+(.+)', line)
                if m:
                    self.frontends[cur_name]['acls'][m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
                    continue
                m = re.match(r'use_backend\s+(\S+)\s+if\s+(\S+)', line)
                if m:
                    self.frontends[cur_name]['rules'].append((m.group(2), m.group(1)))
                    continue
                m = re.match(r'default_backend\s+(\S+)', line)
                if m:
                    self.frontends[cur_name]['default'] = m.group(1)
            elif cur_block == 'backend':
                m = re.match(r'balance\s+(\S+)', line)
                if m:
                    self.backends[cur_name]['balance'] = m.group(1)
                    continue
                m = re.match(r'server\s+(\S+)\s+([\d.]+:\d+)(?:\s+check)?(?:\s+weight\s+(\d+))?', line)
                if m:
                    w = int(m.group(3)) if m.group(3) else 1
                    self.backends[cur_name]['servers'].append(
                        {'name': m.group(1), 'addr': m.group(2), 'weight': w, 'healthy': True, 'conn': 0})

    def eval_acl(self, acl_cond, request):
        """Tiny ACL evaluator: path_beg, hdr(host) -i, src -f."""
        if acl_cond.startswith('path_beg'):
            path = acl_cond.split()[-1]
            return request['path'].startswith(path)
        if acl_cond.startswith('hdr(host)'):
            host_acl = acl_cond.split()[-1]
            return request['host'].lower() == host_acl.lower()
        if acl_cond.startswith('src -f'):
            return request['ip'] in ('192.168.99.99', '10.10.10.10')  # mock blocklist
        return False

    def route(self, frontend_name, request):
        fe = self.frontends[frontend_name]
        for acl_name, backend_name in fe['rules']:
            if self.eval_acl(fe['acls'][acl_name], request):
                return backend_name
        return fe['default']

class HAProxy:
    def __init__(self, conf):
        self.conf = conf
        self.rr_idx = defaultdict(int)

    def pick_server(self, backend_name):
        be = self.conf.backends[backend_name]
        healthy = [s for s in be['servers'] if s['healthy']]
        if not healthy:
            return None
        if be['balance'] == 'roundrobin':
            # weighted round-robin
            pool = []
            for s in healthy:
                pool.extend([s] * s['weight'])
            pick = pool[self.rr_idx[backend_name] % len(pool)]
            self.rr_idx[backend_name] += 1
            return pick
        elif be['balance'] == 'leastconn':
            return min(healthy, key=lambda s: s['conn'])
        return healthy[0]

    def handle_request(self, request):
        be_name = self.conf.route('https_in', request)
        srv = self.pick_server(be_name)
        if not srv:
            return "HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable\r\n\r\n"
        srv['conn'] += 1
        resp = f"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nX-Backend: {srv['name']} ({srv['addr']})\r\n\r\n"
        srv['conn'] -= 1
        return resp

    # Runtime API: change weight without reload
    def set_weight(self, backend, server, weight):
        for s in self.conf.backends[backend]['servers']:
            if s['name'] == server:
                s['weight'] = weight
                print(f"[runtime] {backend}/{server} weight -> {weight}")
                return
        print(f"[runtime] server {backend}/{server} not found")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    conf = HAProxyConfig(HAPROXY_CFG)
    hp = HAProxy(conf)

    # Simulate a stream of requests
    requests = [
        {'ip': '1.2.3.4', 'host': 'api.example.com', 'path': '/api/users'},
        {'ip': '1.2.3.5', 'host': 'api.example.com', 'path': '/api/v2/items'},
        {'ip': '1.2.3.6', 'host': 'admin.example.com', 'path': '/admin/dashboard'},
        {'ip': '1.2.3.7', 'host': 'api.example.com', 'path': '/api/orders'},
        {'ip': '192.168.99.99', 'host': 'api.example.com', 'path': '/api/secure'},  # blocked
    ]
    for r in requests:
        resp = hp.handle_request(r)
        first = resp.splitlines()[0] if resp else "(denied)"
        print(f"{r['ip']:15} {r['host']:25} {r['path']:25} -> {first}")

    # Live weight change via runtime API (no reload)
    print("\n--- runtime API: drain s3 (set weight 0) ---")
    hp.set_weight('api_v1', 's3', 0)
    for _ in range(5):
        r = {'ip': '1.2.3.4', 'host': 'api.example.com', 'path': '/api/test'}
        print(f"  -> {hp.handle_request(r).splitlines()[1]}")
```

HAProxy periodically (every inter seconds, default 2s) sends an HTTP request to the configured path on the server; if it gets a 2xx/3xx response within the timeout, the check passes.
